title: Breaking the $T^{2/3}$ Barrier for Sequential Calibration
abstract: arXiv:2406.13668v4 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: A set of probabilistic forecasts is calibrated if each prediction of the forecaster closely approximates the empirical distribution of outcomes on the subset of timesteps where that prediction was made. We study the fundamental problem of online calibrated forecasting of binary sequences under the standard $\ell_1$ calibration error metric, which was initially studied by Foster & Vohra (1998). They derived an algorithm with $O(T^{2/3})$ calibration error after $T$ time steps, and showed a lower bound of $\Omega(T^{1/2})$. These bounds remained stagnant for two decades, until Qiao & Valiant (2021) improved the lower bound to $\Omega(T^{0.528})$ by introducing a combinatorial game called sign preservation and showing that lower bounds for this game imply lower bounds for calibration. tldr: 本文首次突破了序贯校准问题中 Foster & Vohra 提出的 $O(T^{2/3})$ 校准误差上界，改进了这一停滞二十余年的经典界限。
